name: robotframework
title: Robot Framework
description: Pass camel exchanges to acceptance test written in Robot DSL.
label: testing

properties.name: resourceUri
properties.description: Path to the resource. You can prefix with: classpath, file, http, ref, or bean. classpath, file and http loads the resource using these protocols (classpath is default). ref will lookup the resource in the registry. bean will call a method on a bean to be used as the resource. For bean you can specify the method name after dot, eg bean:myBean.myMethod.

properties.name: allowContextMapAll
properties.description: Sets whether the context map should allow access to all details. By default only the message body and headers can be accessed. This option can be enabled for full access to the current Exchange and CamelContext. Doing so impose a potential security risk as this opens access to the full power of CamelContext API.

properties.name: allowTemplateFromHeader
properties.description: Whether to allow to use resource template from header or not (default false). Enabling this allows to specify dynamic templates via message header. However this can be seen as a potential security vulnerability if the header is coming from a malicious user, so use this with care.

properties.name: argumentFiles
properties.description: A text String to read more arguments from.

properties.name: combinedTagStats
properties.description: Creates combined statistics based on tags. Use the format tags:title List

properties.name: criticalTags
properties.description: Tests that have the given tags are considered critical. List

properties.name: debugFile
properties.description: A debug String that is written during execution.

properties.name: document
properties.description: Sets the documentation of the top-level tests suites.

properties.name: dryrun
properties.description: Sets dryrun mode on use. In the dry run mode tests are run without executing keywords originating from test libraries. Useful for validating test data syntax.

properties.name: excludes
properties.description: Selects the tests cases by tags. List

properties.name: exitOnFailure
properties.description: Sets robot to stop execution immediately if a critical test fails.

properties.name: includes
properties.description: Selects the tests cases by tags. List

properties.name: listener
properties.description: Sets a single listener for monitoring tests execution

properties.name: listeners
properties.description: Sets multiple listeners for monitoring tests execution. Use the format ListenerWithArgs:arg1:arg2 or simply ListenerWithoutArgs List

properties.name: log
properties.description: Sets the path to the generated log String.

properties.name: logLevel
properties.description: Sets the threshold level for logging.

properties.name: logTitle
properties.description: Sets a title for the generated tests log.

properties.name: metadata
properties.description: Sets free metadata for the top level tests suites. comma seperated list of string resulting as List

properties.name: monitorColors
properties.description: Using ANSI colors in console. Normally colors work in unixes but not in Windows. Default is 'on'. 'on' - use colors in unixes but not in Windows 'off' - never use colors 'force' - always use colors (also in Windows)

properties.name: monitorWidth
properties.description: Width of the monitor output. Default is 78.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Sets the name of the top-level tests suites.

properties.name: nonCriticalTags
properties.description: Tests that have the given tags are not critical. List

properties.name: noStatusReturnCode
properties.description: If true, sets the return code to zero regardless of failures in test cases. Error codes are returned normally.

properties.name: output
properties.description: Sets the path to the generated output String.

properties.name: outputDirectory
properties.description: Configures where generated reports are to be placed.

properties.name: randomize
properties.description: Sets the test execution order to be randomized. Valid values are all, suite, and test

properties.name: report
properties.description: Sets the path to the generated report String.

properties.name: reportBackground
properties.description: Sets background colors for the generated report and summary.

properties.name: reportTitle
properties.description: Sets a title for the generated tests report.

properties.name: runEmptySuite
properties.description: Executes tests also if the top level test suite is empty. Useful e.g. with --include/--exclude when it is not an error that no test matches the condition.

properties.name: runFailed
properties.description: Re-run failed tests, based on output.xml String.

properties.name: runMode
properties.description: Sets the execution mode for this tests run. Note that this setting has been deprecated in Robot Framework 2.8. Use separate dryryn, skipTeardownOnExit, exitOnFailure, and randomize settings instead.

properties.name: skipTeardownOnExit
properties.description: Sets whether the teardowns are skipped if the test execution is prematurely stopped.

properties.name: splitOutputs
properties.description: Splits output and log files.

properties.name: suites
properties.description: Selects the tests suites by name. List

properties.name: suiteStatLevel
properties.description: Defines how many levels to show in the Statistics by Suite table in outputs.

properties.name: summaryTitle
properties.description: Sets a title for the generated summary report.

properties.name: tagDocs
properties.description: Adds documentation to the specified tags. List

properties.name: tags
properties.description: Sets the tags(s) to all executed tests cases. List

properties.name: tagStatExcludes
properties.description: Excludes these tags from the Statistics by Tag and Test Details by Tag tables in outputs. List

properties.name: tagStatIncludes
properties.description: Includes only these tags in the Statistics by Tag and Test Details by Tag tables in outputs. List

properties.name: tagStatLinks
properties.description: Adds external links to the Statistics by Tag table in outputs. Use the format pattern:link:title List

properties.name: tests
properties.description: Selects the tests cases by name. List

properties.name: timestampOutputs
properties.description: Adds a timestamp to all output files.

properties.name: variableFiles
properties.description: Sets variables using variables files. Use the format path:args List

properties.name: variables
properties.description: Sets individual variables. Use the format name:value List

properties.name: warnOnSkippedFiles
properties.description: Show a warning when an invalid String is skipped.

properties.name: xunitFile
properties.description: Sets the path to the generated XUnit compatible result String, relative to outputDirectory. The String is in xml format. By default, the String name is derived from the testCasesDirectory parameter, replacing blanks in the directory name by underscores.

properties.name: sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: pollStrategy
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: backoffErrorThreshold
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

properties.name: backoffIdleThreshold
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

properties.name: backoffMultiplier
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

properties.name: delay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Milliseconds before the next poll.

properties.name: greedy
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

properties.name: initialDelay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

properties.name: repeatCount
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

properties.name: runLoggingLevel
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

properties.name: scheduledExecutorService
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

properties.name: scheduler
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

properties.name: schedulerProperties
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

properties.name: startScheduler
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

properties.name: timeUnit
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

properties.name: useFixedDelay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.
